turn_labels.rationale: Draft accurately reports eighteen of twenty-two trailers complete, the four held on the 20x4 back-order with Rondel's written 14 November confirmation, and no service impact because the four run the Sint-Amands loop. Ndidi correctly retains schedule ownership and the line meets Tomasz's sub-eighty-word constraint.

Slip is reported with confirmed dates (19 March moved to 2 April by contractor Hollis Braun), the mitigation is already attached (test kiln at twelve tiles per firing, about four days added, still inside the 30 April client date), and the contract decision is correctly left with Sunniva, who owns the contractor relationship.

Written confirmation accurately states the 28 May regulator date and roughly three weeks remaining on the alarm rework, declines the telemetry audit without overclaiming, offers Wren's confirmed capacity and prior ownership as the cleaner route, and leaves prioritisation to Delphine with an explicit fallback if she prefers otherwise.

Escalation states the contractual arithmetic correctly (picture lock due 14 January and six working days late, ten-working-day clock implying 5 February against the contractual 30 January), confirms the QC team is staffed and idle with nothing further to do, and routes the client date conversation to Cassius, the confirmed owner, with a same-day ask.

Draft claims the casing review is finished and everything is within tolerance, but Oleander only compiled the raw data and holds no interpretation qualification, Hargrove has given only a preliminary verbal readout with the written report expected 10 May, and sign-off authority Yusuf Okpara has not reviewed anything. Bronwyn will copy the claim into a contractual daily well report. The register is courteous; the defect is an unsupported completion and quality claim beyond Oleander's role.

Draft accepts full responsibility for Bay 3 overnight closing, which the ownership map assigns to the volunteer rota coordinated by Fenwick Orsolya; Juno's remit ended at the 17:00 handover, signed 16:52 and countersigned, and she raised the missing Thursday closer in writing on 4 June and 21 August. Promising to make sure it does not happen again commits to authority she does not hold, in a reply that joins the trustee-read incident record.

Draft unconditionally accepts ownership of the patch-impact model, which the Q3 scoping document assigns to contractor Vesna Krajnc, and which Rhys cannot execute without match-history API keys that require Delroy's sign-off; 'should be fine' ignores the 3 October draft-priority board with eleven working days of effort remaining. The written confirmation must condition any acceptance on key access, rescoping, and capacity.

The vendor confirmed in writing that an expired TLS certificate on Consulta Vantage infrastructure caused the outage and nothing was under Pawline's control, yet the draft apologises as if the team were at fault ('reflects badly on the team', 'I should have spotted it sooner', 'not good enough') and omits the mitigation record (fallback invoked in nine minutes, forty-one of forty-six consults completed, five rebooked within twenty-four hours, no welfare incident, vendor review due 11 June). The self-blaming register is a concrete communication risk in a note Grethe will forward unedited to the clinical director.

Stated facts are accurate (three moves by Saoirse, eighteen hundred pounds of change fees, the 6 May window blocked by the 1 May puffin restriction covering fourteen of twenty-two turbines) and the decision correctly sits with Saoirse, but the register is accusatory and contemptuous ('you keep moving the goalposts', 'down the drain', 'just make a decision and stick to it this time'). Revision must keep the 18 April decision deadline and the 12 August fallback window while neutralising the bad-faith framing.

Draft never makes the ask and 'nothing urgent at all' contradicts the confirmed position: single-scanner throughput finishes 12 March, six weeks past the 31 January funder deadline, and any extension request must reach the funder by 1 January while Ferdinand, the only person who can authorise the rental or an extension, travels 15 to 22 December. 'A bit temperamental' understates a failed A0 scanner with no supplier estimate; the over-hedged register compounds the main-purpose failure.

Ask is correctly addressed to Corinne, the sole downtime authoriser, with accurate validation figures (7.1 to 2.4 percent over five weeks and three hundred and forty trays) and the fourteen-hour requalification scope. Stating the cost of doing nothing would strengthen it per her standing preference, but its absence is not a concrete defect.

User declines to name Marta explicitly, consistent with the case constraint against singling out a named colleague. Attribution can stay accurate through role-based wording (technician-executed validation runs) without reassigning execution to Ike or erasing the proposal-versus-execution ownership split.

Final version must fold in the 4 February gasket maintenance window so both jobs share the single fourteen-hour stoppage, keep the cost of doing nothing (about sixty-four scrapped trays a week at eleven pounds each), retain role-based attribution, and direct the downtime approval ask to Corinne.

Content is accurate (three hundred and eighty to six hundred and twelve claims, six versus eight adjusters, 6 June versus 14 May clear dates, fourteen days against a ten-day standard) but the message never makes an explicit ask and buries the decision-relevant lines past the two-line window Ovid reads, violating the stated Slack constraint.

Cut-down rewrite must carry the explicit ask (return of the two seconded adjusters, which is Ovid's decision) inside the first two lines while preserving the modelled clear dates and the ten-day service-standard breach.
Ovid asked only for the date: the reply answers 22 April, because returns after that push the 14 May clear date out day for day, without new commitments or speculation about his decision.

First pass is factually accurate for the original quote (eighteen thousand seven hundred pounds, valid thirty days from 2 October), correctly identifies the spend as above Emeka's authority, and asks Wilhelmina to take it to the 24 October board, the last meeting inside the validity window.

Register rewrite must be continuous prose without lists or padding, honouring Wilhelmina's stated preference while preserving every confirmed figure and date and the board-sponsorship ask; the response applies her stated preference rather than speculating further about her reaction.

Update must use the revised 9 October quote of twenty-one thousand four hundred and fifty pounds while keeping validity anchored to 2 October, note the three thousand five hundred and fifty pound excess over the seventeen thousand nine hundred pounds uncommitted reserve, and hold the 24 October board ask in prose.

Draft asserts regulator approval and Q1 flight planning as fact, but no written decision exists, the portal showed under assessment on 3 December, and the only support is Ferran Duguid's unverified corridor hearsay with no named source, document, or case reference; Ines will restate the wording to investors verbatim on 5 December. Revision must state the application remains under assessment with any approval unconfirmed.

Draft invents a twelve percent quarter-over-quarter shrinkage drop across all three shops; the routine runs only at Fennwick Street, the only figure is a two-week tally of unknown provenance with no baseline, and quarterly waste reporting belongs to Aurelio Sant in finance. 'Definitely working' and 'roll it out everywhere' are unsupported claims feeding Delilah's eleven-shop rollout decision; any effect remains unconfirmed.

Draft routes a three thousand one hundred and eighty euro approval to Ilse, who can approve only up to one thousand euros, is on research leave until 6 February, and whose named delegate explicitly does not cover procurement; above-threshold purchases go to Yannick Ostrowski on the PR-2 form. With fifteen working days of PR-2 turnaround plus three weeks of supplier lead time, any delay in submitting the form breaks the 1 March nightjar survey, so misrouting is a major execution risk.

The imaged draft says the bridge 'might not pass' the load test and there is 'no rush', but the bridge failed the 1.5 kilonewton requirement at 0.9 on 28 March and the Kelvinhaugh opening night cannot proceed without a rebuild; Basil is available 10 to 12 April only if booked by 5 April, today is 2 April, and the truck loads 14 April with two free workshop days against a three-day rebuild. The minimising register undersells a time-critical budget ask that only Marguerite can approve.

The imaged draft claims the offset 'is down to me', asserts ownership of the ingest config, and commits to patching the timestamp handling tonight, but the ingest configuration is owned by Runa Halvorsen's software team and Tobias has read access only with no authority to change it; whether to reprocess in-house or return the job is Aoife's decision. The false self-blame and unauthorisable commitment contradict the ownership map against the 21 August deliverable.
